newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain, China close to HK troops deal - paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain, China close to HK troops deal - paper.

text.p: Britain and China are close to an agreement allowing an advance party of Chinese troops to move into Hong Kong before London hands back the colony to Beijing this year, a Hong Kong newspaper said on Wednesday.

The South China Morning Post quoted Chinese senior officers who gave media a tour of military and naval facilities in the south China port of Shantou as saying the advance troops would not carry weapons.

"I believe the question will be settled very soon," Colonel Li Xiuhong, commander of a Chinese Navy unit which will be based in Hong Kong when China takes over on July 1, said at the Shantou base when asked how soon an agreement would be reached.
The size and function of the advance unit and whether or not the personnel will be armed has been under discussion in diplomatic talks between the two countries.
The latest session is currently under way in London.

Major-General Liu Zhenwu, who will head the People's Liberation Army garrison in Hong Kong, told the reporters the advance guard would not bring weapons when they arrive in Hong Kong to prepare the ground for the garrison troops.
The Chinese Navy showed the reporters several vessels, including four guided-missile frigates, during the visit.
The unit of nearly 20 vessels will cruise Hong Kong waters after the handover.
